name_reason: Name follows the fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention and accurately describes the function: an interactive input loop that waits for the player to pick an action target tile/char. No Ghidra address residue. Confirmed against all four callers (player movement-tile pick, attack target, item give/use, spell target).
purpose: Interactive cursor input loop that lets the player choose a target tile/char for a battle action; returns 1 when a valid target is committed and -1 on ESC cancel.
logic_summary: target_iter=0. For mode==6 the n_options slot actually carries the caster self-index (saved to self_idx_in_mode6) and n_options is forced to 0. Reads battle_anim_phase into anim_phase_ref (decremented if >1) for the in-range scan. If n_options>0 it pans the cursor to pTarget_array[0] (unless that char's portrait_id==0x79). Then loops on fd2_wait_for_input_v2(): ESC(0x01)->return -1; SPACE(0x39)/ENTER(0x1c) attempts to commit per mode -- mode 6: keep looping if a living non-self ally occupies the cursor tile, else commit only if the job's movement-cost table marks the cursor's terrain attribute as passable (not 0x14); mode 5 always loops; other modes require the tile_map passability byte (offset+7) != 0xFF, and (unless mode==4) require fd2_scan_chars_within_manhattan_range to find at least one target, then commit. Z(0x2c)/keypad(0x4c) cycles target_iter through pTarget_array[0..n_options-1] (wrapping to 0) and re-pans. Arrow scancodes (0x48/0x50/0x4b/0x4d) move the cursor and play a step SFX. Any other key is ignored.
signature: int __cdecl fd2_wait_for_action_target_input(int mode, uint32 n_options, uint8 *pTarget_array)

params.name: mode
params.semantics: Action-mode selector driving the commit policy. Observed caller values: 0 = attack target (tile passable + at least one char in manhattan range); 3 = give-item-to-ally target (other-branch, same passable+in-range rule); 4 = movement destination tile (passable only, skips the in-range scan); 5 = single-target spell with no AoE targets available (always loops, never commits); 6 = spell/teleport target (commit only if no living ally at cursor AND terrain passable); other values come from an item/spell aoe_kind or aoe_pattern byte and take the default other-branch.
params.reason: Accurate and descriptive of its role as the behavior selector; no address residue.

params.name: n_options
params.semantics: Number of candidate targets in pTarget_array that Z/keypad cycles through. Special case: when mode==6 the caller instead passes the caster's own char index here, which the body moves into self_idx_in_mode6 and then zeroes n_options (no cycling in mode 6).
params.reason: Reflects the dominant meaning (count of cyclable target options for modes 0/3/4/other). The mode-6 overload (self-index) is documented in the comment; renaming to favor the overload would misname the common path. No address residue.

params.name: pTarget_array
params.semantics: Pointer to an array of candidate target char-indices used for the Z/keypad cycle and the initial cursor pan. NULL for modes (4 and 6) that do not cycle a precomputed list.
params.reason: Accurate pointer-to-target-array name with correct p-prefix; no address residue.

returns.semantics: 1 = target committed (caller proceeds with the action); -1 = ESC cancelled. No other return values.
